quotes.verbatim_quote:
Volume II contains 3-part 4ths, 4-part 4ths and spread clusters voice-led through all 6
cycles in C Major, C Melodic Minor and C Harmonic Minor. If we add this material to all the
material in Volume I, we have “The Mother Lode.” (We'll start referring to it as the M-Lode...)
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines scope and name of the M-Lode system.

quotes.verbatim_quote:

TBN I

quotes.why_load_bearing: Master taxonomy of chord families across both volumes.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
If you look at all of the material in Volume I, you would see that
it’s all triad-based. The triads are triads. The 7th chords are a triad plus another note. TBN Lis a
triad plus another note. And TBN II is also a triad plus another note.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Unifying structural principle of Volume I.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
you've got the complete set of 5 families of 4-part chords: 7th, TBN I, TBN IL, 4
part 4th, Spread Cluster.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Closed exhaustive list of 4-part chord families.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
It would seem that the main focus is on 4-part structures and that the 3-part structures
are used as “supplements.”
